name: Centro Historico (Largo das Forras and Matriz)
description: The postcard core around the Largo das Forras square and the gilded Matriz de Santo Antonio church. Cobbled lanes lined with colonial mansions, artisan shops, cafes, and the town's celebrated restaurants sit within an easy walk. Beautiful and central, though busiest and priciest on weekends.
bestFor: First-time visitors and food-loving slow travelers

name: Sao Francisco de Paula (Upper Town)
description: The upper reaches of town around the Sao Francisco de Paula church, climbing the hillside above the historic core. A calmer, more residential feel with lovely rooftop views over the colonial rooftops and mountains, yet still a short if steep walk down to the squares and restaurants below.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting quiet with views
pros: Great views over town and hills
Still close to the center on foot

name: Toward the Serra de Sao Jose
description: The edge of town along the roads leading toward the Serra de Sao Jose, where pousadas and homes give way to trailheads, greenery, and waterfalls. A peaceful, nature-first base for hikers and anyone wanting cool air and birdsong, with the historic center a walk or short drive away.
bestFor: Hikers and those craving quiet and nature
cons: Best with a car for convenience

name: Sao Joao del Rei (nearby base)
description: A bigger historic city about 12km away, linked to Tiradentes by the charming Maria Fumaca steam train and regular buses. It offers more services, shops, bus connections, and a small airport, plus its own baroque churches and lively streets, making it a practical base for longer or more connected stays.
bestFor: Those needing more services and transport links
